senses.gloss:
Periyapurāṇam
(‘the great purāṇa [mythological work]’)
------------------------------------------
The sixtythree Nāyanmārs or नायनार्स् are the Śaiva saints of Tamil Nadu who spread the cult of devotion to Lord शिव (as an aspect of ब्रह्मन्, the Absolute), brought about a social revolution that made all devotees of Lord शिव feel equal to one another and also contri-buted to the disappearance of जैनिस्म् from the Tamil land.
Their lives were found in a sketchy form loosely distributed among various works and hearsays.
However, it was Sekkizhār (11th cent. A. D.) who brought together all the available information about these Nāyanmārs in one place and wrote the now well-known classic the Periyapurāṇam. He based his work on Tiru Toṇḍattokai of सुन्दरमूर्ति (8th cent. A. D.) and the Tirutoṇḍar Tiruvandādi of Nambiandar Nambi (10th cent. A. D.).
The Periyapurāṇam is a remarkable composite work of hagiology dealing with all the 63 lives. It is in 72 cantos and has 4286 verses.
The biographies of the four most well-known saints—Sundarar, Tirujñāna सम्बन्धर्, अप्पर् and Tirumūlar—are dealt with in great detail. The others have been portrayed briefly.
This work is also a literary master-piece. Good English translations of the works have been published in the recent past.
See also NĀYANĀRS.
